evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.text: The entry records 點 as composed of 黑 with 占 as phonetic, with the original sense ‘small black mark’. Its form listings show a seal-script example but no oracle-bone or bronze examples for 點. The related 占 entry has oracle-bone examples and explains that graph as 卜 plus 口, used for interpreting divination cracks; that is evidence for 占’s own history, not for an early 點 graph.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：點

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.text: The entry gives 《晉書·文苑傳·袁宏》 ‘如彼白珪，質無塵點’ as an example of 點, and cites 《爾雅·釋器》 ‘滅謂之點’ with a note that writing over a character could be called 點. It also cites examples for ornamenting from a Wei-period fu, punctuation/句讀 from the Southern Song-era text 《世說新語·文學》, a liquid drop from a Song poem, and checking/counting from a Tang poem. These cited examples indicate separately attested uses; their sequence in the entry does not by itself establish when or how each sense developed.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：點

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.text: The 占 entry describes oracle-bone forms as 卜 plus 口, with variant arrangements and a form in which the mouth element is reduced; it gives the use ‘王占’ in 《合集》21068 and ‘王占曰：吉’ in 《合集》116反. It lists Middle Chinese fanqie readings 職廉 (level tone) and 章豔 (departing tone), corresponding to modern Mandarin zhān and zhàn. These records attest 占’s forms and uses independently; they do not establish that 點 was graphically present in oracle-bone or bronze inscriptions.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：占

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: pronunciation comparison for 點 and 占
evidence.text: For 點, the entry gives Guangyun 多忝切 and Middle Chinese initials/final/tone categories 端母, 添/忝 rhyme, rising tone, Division IV. 占 has 職廉切 in level tone and 章豔切 in departing tone, with Middle Chinese 章母, 鹽 rhyme, Division III. Thus the reconstructed historical comparison depends on the system and reading; the modern Mandarin readings diǎn versus zhān/zhàn are not close, and the consulted source does not supply an Old Chinese reconstruction for both words on the same system. The phonetic classification is the dictionary’s explicit analysis, while the exact sound history cannot be independently reconstructed from this entry alone.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：點

evidence.text: The 点 entry identifies 点 as the simplified form of 點 and classifies its structure as top-bottom, from 灬 with 占 as phonetic. The traditional 點 entry instead identifies 黑 as the semantic component and 占 as phonetic. This records the modern component analysis and simplified/traditional correspondence; it does not establish that 灬 was the original semantic component in the historical 點 graph.
evidence.title: 点 diǎn - 汉典

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: traditional graph, variant forms, pronunciation and senses
evidence.text: The entry names 點 the standard form, gives the Shuowen explanation 小黑也。从黑，占聲 and fanqie 多忝切, and lists 点 among its variant forms. It records senses including small trace, liquid drop, punctuation or textual marking, designation, checking, lighting, and point as a time or measure unit, citing texts such as 《說文》, 《爾雅》, Tang poetry, and 《木蘭詩》. Its variant listing establishes a graphic relationship but does not by itself date the creation of 点.
evidence.title: A04775 點 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.text: For 點, the entry records Middle Chinese 端母 忝韻 上聲, 多忝切; it gives Tang-period reading *děm, Cantonese dim2, Japanese on-reading TEN and kun-reading BOCHI, Korean 점 (romanized CEM), and Vietnamese điểm. It also reports Old Chinese categories under Huang Kan and Wang Li, but provides no same-system comparison for 占. These are readings of the character, not evidence for the original pronunciation of a depicted object.

evidence.text: The 占 entry lists Middle Chinese fanqie 職廉切 and 章豔切. These correspond to separate readings zhān and zhàn in modern Mandarin. It does not provide a same-system Old Chinese reconstruction comparison with 點 in the inspected passage.

evidence.text: The entry cites 點 in Jin-period 《晉書·文苑傳·袁宏》 in the sense of an unblemished white jade with no spot; it also quotes 《爾雅·釋器》 with Guo Pu’s gloss linking 點 to writing over a character. Further examples are attributed to Wei-period writing for ornamenting, Southern Song 《世說新語》 for textual punctuation, a Song poem for raindrops, and a Tang poem for checking/counting. These separate citations do not by themselves establish a chronological chain of semantic change.

gaps: No inspected source supplied securely dated earliest attestations of 點 as an inscriptional graph; the CUHK entry lists no oracle-bone or bronze examples, while the seal-script and Shuowen evidence establish a later graphic witness without specifying an exact earliest date.

The earliest lexical use is not conclusively fixed by the consulted material. Shuowen’s gloss ‘small black [mark]’ and later cited texts support that sense, but the sources do not provide a complete corpus chronology.

The sources document multiple later uses—staining, textual marking, drops, ornamenting, counting, time units, and other senses—but do not establish a continuous, dated chain of semantic change for every extension.

The component relation is securely reported as 黑 semantic plus 占 phonetic in traditional 點. No independent same-system Old Chinese reconstructions for 點 and the relevant 占 reading were inspected, so the exact historical sound match cannot be quantified here.

Modern simplified 点 uses 灬 graphically where traditional 點 has 黑; do not transfer traditional component analysis literally onto the simplified shape. The looked-up sources support simplification/variant correspondence but do not determine the full historical graphic path or precise adoption date for 点.

No whole-graph phonetic-loan account or depicted-object borrowing claim was supported by the inspected authoritative sources. The dossier’s unrelated ‘fusion’ note was not corroborated and is not used as an etymology.

No glyph image is proposed: the relevant Commons category result did not establish an inspectable file description page, exact image URL, and reuse-rights statement for 點-seal.svg. The direct Commons page attempts failed, and the exact Xiaoxuetang 点-specific record could not be loaded.

The inspected CUHK entry provides no securely dated earliest inscriptional 點 witness in its listings; it shows one small-seal example but no oracle-bone or bronze forms. Its database’s absent entries do not prove the character never occurred in those script traditions.
The earliest lexical attestation is not fixed here. The sources cite a Shuowen definition and later-attributed classical examples, but do not supply a complete corpus chronology.

The cited senses include spot, textual marking or erasure, ornamenting, drop, and checking/counting. Their examples are attributed to different works and periods, but the sources do not establish every semantic transition between them.

Although the database explicitly analyzes 占 as 點’s phonetic component, the inspected same-source Middle Chinese categories differ. No independently verified same-system Old Chinese comparison for both relevant readings was obtained, so the historical sound correspondence remains unresolved.

The modern simplified 点 corresponds to traditional 點, but the inspected references do not establish its complete graphic development or a precise adoption date. Do not treat the present 灬 shape as proof that fire was the original semantic component.
No source inspected here supports a whole-graph phonetic loan or borrowing based on the name of a depicted object. The repository’s unrelated fusion note remains uncorroborated.
